zuregex

zuregex is a regular expression package that matches with a bundled PCRE2, the same version on every platform, from R and from C.

Base R’s perl = TRUE uses PCRE2 too. zuregex adds what that leaves out:

  • Capture groups come back as a data frame, one column per group.
  • A pattern is compiled once and cached, and matching runs on several threads where the build has OpenMP.
  • Replacements use PCRE2’s full template language: groups by name, past nine, with defaults and case forcing.
  • Other packages reach the same PCRE2 from C through LinkingTo, instead of bundling a copy.

Installation

Install zuregex from CRAN with:

install.packages("zuregex")

Or install the development version from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuregex")

Usage 

library(zuregex)

re_match() turns the named groups of a pattern into the columns of a data frame, one row per string. The last string is not a log line, so its row is NA.

log <- c(
  "2026-10-21 08:15:02 GET /index.html 200 512",
  "2026-10-21 08:15:09 POST /login 302 0",
  "2026-10-21 08:16:44 GET /missing 404 128",
  "not a log line"
)
pattern <- "(?<time>\\S+ \\S+) (?<method>[A-Z]+) (?<path>\\S+) (?<status>\\d+)"
re_match(log, pattern)
#>                  time method        path status
#> 1 2026-10-21 08:15:02    GET /index.html    200
#> 2 2026-10-21 08:15:09   POST      /login    302
#> 3 2026-10-21 08:16:44    GET    /missing    404
#> 4                <NA>   <NA>        <NA>   <NA>

zuregex also detects, extracts, replaces and splits with the same patterns; Get started walks through them on this log.

Learn more

  • Get started takes the log above through every main function.
  • Move from base R and stringr maps grepl(), sub(), regmatches() and the str_*() functions onto re_*(), and shows what behaves differently.
  • Bound the work of a match sets match, depth and heap limits for patterns or input you do not trust.
  • Link to zuregex from C uses the bundled PCRE2 from another package’s C code.
  • The reference index lists every function, grouped as the API is.

zuregex builds on PCRE2, which backtracks. For matching in linear time, use re2.
